dossier.architecture: Pivoting telescopic arm with compact roller gripper and added cone-centering floor intake.

subsystems.intake: Low-pivot floor collector centers tipped cones with mecanum/omni rollers and presents them for handoff.
subsystems.transfer: Collector rotates the centered cone into a narrow gripper; handoff angle adjusted to match hardware revisions.
subsystems.scoring: Pivoting, extending arm with low transmission and an absolute encoder measuring actual arm angle beyond gearbox backlash.
subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve with runtime generated drive-to-point paths.
subsystems.endgame: Autonomous modes include station traversal, retrieval and balance.
subsystems.controls: Safe arm waypoints avoid grid collisions; dashboard exposes piece/level selection and adjustable scoring setpoints.

versions: First event lacked the cone floor intake.
Earlier concept included a spindexer, which influenced the narrow gripper geometry.
Team credits Team 95 for floor-intake inspiration.
dossier.analysis: Study the way an added acquisition capability fits a pre-existing arm. A centered handoff can preserve a small gripper rather than forcing the entire wrist to become full width.
limits: Intermediate prototype and competition dates are not fully resolved.

context_documents.body:
# 2023-1577: A compliant collector must hand off at the actual revised arm geometry

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A low-pivot collector uses mecanum/omni contact to center a tipped cone, then rotates it toward a narrow gripper. The extending scoring arm keeps its transmission low and measures actual arm angle beyond gearbox backlash. Shoulder-style bearing support helps retain bearings in flexible plates.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly credits Grasshoppers inspiration, seeks fast/light centering and explains the low collector pivot as letting impacts lift the mechanism rather than break it. Handoff angle changes must follow hardware revisions.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A wide pickup can improve acquisition while increasing the range of states presented to a narrow receiver. Compliance helps survive contact but must not erase the repeatable pose needed for transfer. Measuring the joint after transmission backlash improves observability; it does not mechanically remove the backlash.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test handoff after collector impacts, compare actual and motor-side angle under reversals, and verify bearing retention after repeated plate flex.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.
